source.title: The Discrete-Log Clock: How a Transformer Learns Modular Multiplication

page_placements.theme: Task-aligned algebraic circuits and their limits

record.file_problem: None noted; the full paper text, including the appendix, is present.
record.tranche_reason: It repeats the train/test grokking experiment on a new modular-arithmetic task, using the reported Nanda et al. setup and training measures, and reports results bearing on delayed generalization.
record.gate_note: The paper reports a grokking curve for modular multiplication, but does not sweep training-set size. It analyzes the learned mechanism at a grokked checkpoint rather than tracking circuit formation over training, so those mechanistic measurements do not test V2's gradual-progress claim. Its discussion of weight decay is not an ablation or a test of critical dataset size. Results attributed to prior work are not included as rows.
record.test_reason: It reruns the Nanda et al. (2023) grokking setup (same architecture, 30% data, AdamW, weight decay 1.0) on a·b mod 113 and reports train and test loss over training, so its results bear on V1. Multi-seed mechanism results bear on V6. Most rows are post-hoc mechanistic measurements at one grokked checkpoint.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude the 'dense spectrum' reported for multiplication is a basis artifact, and that the model implements a Discrete-Log Clock: multiplication reduced to addition in log space, then Nanda's trig mechanism. They report it recurs across ~80% of seeds and 10 primes. They assert, without testing, that weight decay drives the memorization-to-generalization transition, and do not claim the algorithm is unique.
record.recipe_differences: The authors say the architecture and hyperparameters follow Nanda et al. (2023), but change the task to modular multiplication mod 113. The tested model uses 30% training data and weight decay 1.0.
record.method_sensitivity: The embedding and neuron-spectrum results differ substantially between the additive and multiplicative Fourier bases. Across random seeds, the reported Gini coefficient varies from 0.45–0.61 and key frequencies vary.

fits_no_version.finding: The embedding spectrum of the grokked multiplication model is sparse in the multiplicative character basis (Gini 0.579, 4 key frequencies) and flat in the additive basis (Gini 0.071, 0 key frequencies).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Grokked modular-multiplication transformers learn a sparse Fourier representation in discrete-log coordinates.

fits_no_version.finding: 496/512 neurons are single-frequency tuned in the multiplicative basis versus 0/512 in the additive basis; mean max-fraction is 0.925 vs 0.054.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: MLP neurons in modular-multiplication models are tuned to single multiplicative characters.

fits_no_version.finding: Discrete-log ordering reveals diagonal stripes in neuron heatmaps and sinusoidal SVD components; embedding effective rank is 10.3 of 112.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Discrete-log ordering exposes periodic structure in learned modular-multiplication representations.

fits_no_version.finding: Across 10 primes (p=59–113), the authors report sparse multiplicative spectra with 4–7 key frequencies.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The Discrete-Log Clock recurs across prime moduli.

record.peer_reviewed: Mechanistic Interpretability Workshop at the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning, 2026
record.problems: The reported grokking curve is for one stated task, one training fraction, and one weight-decay setting. The text does not give a training-set-size sweep, the number of random seeds, or uncertainty estimates. The mechanism is not shown to be unique; the paper says so explicitly.
record.rows_left_out: The preliminary modular-exponentiation result (100% accuracy on ab mod 41) is not included because it concerns a different operation and does not report delayed generalization relevant to these versions. No other qualifying results were left out.

untested.parts: Whether the delay grows as the training set shrinks; only 30% training data was used.
Not tested: circuit formation and memorization removal are not tracked over training, and no progress measures are given. The 'gradually favoring' wording is an assertion.
No non-algorithmic data; no sweep of initialization scale or weight norm.
The weight-decay explanation is asserted, not tested. No weight-decay ablation, critical dataset size or ungrokking.
Architectures and hyperparameters are not varied; only seeds (and primes) are.
Only AdamW is used; no optimizer or numerical-precision controls.

record.verdict_notes: The record gave V6 both supports and limits_scope for the same condition group. I merged these into one limits_scope label, since there is only one condition group and the effect holds in ~80% of seeds. Varying key frequencies across seeds is consistent with Nanda et al. and does not by itself contradict V6. The study is not an original source. It is a short workshop paper with no seed counts, error bars or training-fraction sweep, and the grokking curve (Figure 1) is described only in words.

versions.untested_parts: The paper tests delayed generalization for one stated training fraction and task, but does not test whether the delay grows as the training set shrinks.
It does not track circuit formation or memorizing components over time, or test whether continuous progress measures anticipate the test-accuracy jump.
No non-algorithmic data or initialization-scale/weight-norm sweep is tested.
No LLM pretraining or fine-tuning on realistic data is tested.
The paper reports one weight-decay setting and offers an explanation, but does not test the efficiency account, vary the bias toward low norm, or test critical dataset size or ungrokking.
It reports results across random seeds for p=113, but does not compare architectures or hyperparameters.
It does not test adaptive-optimizer instability, softmax numerical limits, or whether controlling them removes the delay.
